headline: Every bag of feed checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: Southern Stockfeeds makes over 180,000 tonnes of tailored pellet feed a year at its Bridgewater mill and is Feedsafe accredited. Most of it leaves in bulk, but wherever feed goes into bags, every bag needs the right ration label and batch code. This is what a camera check could look like after a bagger. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every bag is closed straight across, with no open corners or split tops. A bag that opens in the truck or the shed means wasted feed and a call from the farm.
labelLede: Rations made for different herds look the same in the bag. The camera checks every bag carries the right label for the ration, straight and intact.
codeLede: The batch code is how a bag is traced back to the mill. The system reads the printed batch code and date on every bag and compares them with the ration and batch set at changeover.
objectLede: String, bag offcuts and pallet splinters can all end up on the bag conveyor. The camera spots anything that should not be there before bags are stacked.

vocab.alert: Four crooked closures in fifteen minutes. Check the bag closer.
